answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a ripple as the anchor of the cost.
